title: equal matter
oneLiner: An interactive installation in which human, machine and material take part as equals.

cover.alt: A hand touches the water; bright ring-shaped light reflections ripples.

facts.Context: Future of Making, M.A. Design & Future Making, Pforzheim University
facts.Role: concept, code, setup and physical computing, documentation and paper (50/50)
facts.Tools: capacitive sensing, Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W, Python, speaker, webcam, 3D printing

sections.label: Question
text: How can human, machine and material collaborate as equals, so that none of the three takes a superior role? equal matter explores this question as an interactive installation built around a bowl of water.

media.alt: Two visitors stand at the equal matter installation and touch the water in the bowl. Behind them, the gallery of previous rings are being projected. On the right a 3D printer is printing the ring shapes.

sections.label: Interaction
text: Visitors touch the water. A capacitive sensor reads the gesture and translates it into continuously changing sound frequencies. The water starts to vibrate, and shifting wave patterns appear on its surface. They distort the reflection of a ring light, which a camera captures in real time. From these fleeting configurations the system generates images and 3D models: the reflections become shapes that are printed and turned into silver-plated rings, material traces of a moment in which human gesture, machine behavior and material response meet.

media.alt: Close-up from above: a hand moves in the water, a white light reflection bends on the surface.
A visitor touches the vibrating water, its surface covered in fine wave patterns. On the floor, plotted lettering reads “interact with the water”.

sections.label: Material
text: Building it meant listening to the water. We tested frequencies systematically and found that between roughly 48 and 80 Hz the water answers in patterns that are readable and distinct from each other, so the material itself helps decide the range of the interaction. A gallery next to the installation shows every captured moment as it happens.

media.alt: In a darkened room, a projection shows the gallery of previous rings generated, the bowl stands in the foreground under a lamp.
A small 3D-printed and silverplated ring hangs on a thin thread in front of the blurred projection of the gallery.

consent: Persons shown may be shown (Feli, 13.11.2026, E12).
